title: Staining of Fish Red Blood Cells
author: Robson Andrade Rodrigues
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bd9yi97w
materials: Analyse cells in image analysis software, such as ImageJ or Motic Image Plus FIJI (Image J) NIH Motic Images Plus 2.0 Windows and macOS Motic

steps.title: Prepare MGGW Stain Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the May-Grünwald-Giemsa-Wright (MGGW) stain stock solution and allow it to age.

substeps.instruction: Dilute 1 g of eosin methyl blue of May-Grünwald, 1 g of eosin methyl blue of Giemsa, and 1 g eosin methyl blue of Wright in 1 L of methanol (Methanol P212121 Catalog #PA-33900HPLCCS4L).
Store the stock solution at 25 °C for at least 1 week.
Dilute 3 g of EDTA powder (Merck MilliporeSigma Catalog #E9884) in 100 mL of distilled water.
Load the solution into a 24 G x 3/4” (20 mm x 0.55 mm) 1 mL syringe.

steps.title: Extract Fish Blood
steps.instruction: Collect blood from the fish specimen based on its size.

substeps.instruction: For large specimens, extract blood from the vena caudalis or by cardiac puncture using the EDTA syringe.
For small specimens, extract blood by decaptation and use a 1 µL pipette to collect one drop of blood from the head.

steps.title: Create Blood Smear
steps.instruction: Prepare a blood smear on a microscope slide.

substeps.instruction: Place one drop of blood onto a microscope slide.
Touch a second microscope slide to the blood drop at a 45º angle.
Slide the second slide forward until the drop is fully spread.

steps.title: Apply MGGW Stain
steps.instruction: Apply the MGGW stain to the slide and dilute it.

substeps.instruction: Drop approximately 300 µL of the filtered MGGW stain solution onto the slide until it is fully covered.
Add drops of distilled water to the slide to dilute the stain.
Homogenize the solution on the slide using a plastic straw or a Pasteur pipette until a fine, shiny layer of stain precipitate appears.

steps.title: Wash Slide
steps.instruction: Wash the slides in tap water for 15 seconds.
